newsitem.title: USA: MGE SPRING WHEAT ENDS LOWER AMID HEDGE PRESSURE.
newsitem.headline: MGE SPRING WHEAT ENDS LOWER AMID HEDGE PRESSURE.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures settled lower amid seasonal hedge pressure related to the spring wheat harvest and on followthrough selling from Tuesday's lower close.
Traders said wheat was still feeling pressure from USDA's forecast early Tuesday of a larger than expected 1997 U.S. wheat crop.
USDA Tuesday said the 1997 U.S. crop totalled 2.531 billion bushels, above the July government outlook for 2.431 billion and above an average of analysts' estimates for 2.476 billion.
But wheat also saw pressure from hedging tied to the unfolding harvest in the northern Plains. Wheat drew further spillover weakness from CBOT corn, which was subject to aggressive selling Wednesday.
MGE spring wheat futures settled 1-1/2 to three cents per bushel lower, with September down three cents at $3.91-1/4.

Cargill Investor Services was a featured player, selling 1.2 million December but also buying 1.1 million Sept. Traders said CIS was buying MGE March on the spread with Kansas City. Country Hedging sold one million Sept.
The MGE estimated Wednesday's volume at 24.411 million bushels, down from 25.685 million Tuesday.
